channel.title: Edwin Hwu
channel.description:
Professor, are you seriously telling us to break our gaming consoles for science? Yes, I am :)

I'm Edwin En-Te Hwu, Associate Professor at DTU Health Tech, where I lead MIDAS (Micro Medical Devices and Hardware Hacking Based Technologies) in the IDUN section. videos.t: Repurposing Optical Pickup Units from CD/DVD/Blu-ray Drives for Research
videos.desc:
This video shows how I hack the optical pickup unit (OPU) from CD, DVD and Blu-ray drives for scientific research, such as cell imaging, micro-hole machining, bioassay sensing and atomic force microscopy (AFM) nano-imaging.

An OPU packs lasers, precision optics and voice coil actuators into a tiny, low-cost module, which makes it a fun starting point for lab instruments.

More OPU hacking work in these open-access papers:

1. Hacking CD/DVD/Blu-ray for Biosensing
https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acssensors.8b00340

2. Using DVD optics for Nano-, Micro-, Milli-Newton to several Newtons for

videos.t: 2021 European Inventor Award: Hacked Blu-ray for Cutting Edge Biomedical Diagnostics
videos.desc:
European patent office announced 2021 European #InventorAward that BluSense Diagnostics BluBox is among the top 3 Research Innovation: Hacked Blu-ray drive + Lab on a Disc + Magnetic Nanobeads = Cutting Edge Biomedical Diagnostics for Everyone.

The cost-effective BluBox is beneficial to be widespread for high precision #denguefever #zika and #covidー19 diagnosis. Looking forward to seeing further development of this technology.

This article reveals the secret why BluBox got top three 2021 European Award: https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acssensors.8b00340

videos.t: 2021 IDUN Intro Video (old fashion)
2021 IDUN Intro Video
videos.desc:
About IDUN (https://idun.dtu.dk/)
The center for Intelligent Drug delivery and sensing Using microcontainers and Nanomechanics (IDUN) is a center of excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation and the Villum Foundation. The center is divided into two parts: IDUN Drug and IDUN Sensor, focusing on drug delivery and nanomechanical sensors, respectively.

videos.t: Low Cost Open Source Ultra High Vacuum Nanopositioner Piezoelectric Piezo motor
videos.desc:
12 types of open source low cost 3D printable nanopositioners (piezo electric motor, linear actuator), from thumb-size actuator to 18 axes nano-probing station, used in German National Metrology Institute (PTB), Danish Technical University (DTU), National Taiwan University (NTU), Academia Sinica, etc...

Mechanical/electrical CAD and Arduino-based controller designs are now published in Hardware X and make it open source for everyone.

videos.t: APELLA: Miniaturized Lab-on-a-Disc from Hacked Consumer Electronics
videos.desc:
What do you get when you hack a quadcopter, Qi wireless chargers and a spy camera? APELLA: an open-source, miniaturized, all-in-one powered lab-on-a-disc platform.

It looks like a toy, but it captures rapid mixing events in microfluidic discs that usually need bulky, expensive strobe imaging systems. At about 100 euros, APELLA is light and compact enough to fit in your bag, and it uses less than 6% of the power of conventional systems. Handy for fieldwork, classrooms and resource-limited labs :)

APELLA was developed at the IDUN section, DTU Health Tech, and is published in HardwareX: https:/

videos.t: AFMD Mk1 operation manual by Ellen Raun
Tape Stripping Method for Skin Sampling: AFM Nanotexture Analysis
videos.desc:
Ellen Raun demonstrates the tape stripping method: gently collecting corneocytes from the outermost layer of the skin (stratum corneum) with adhesive tape. The samples can then be scanned with atomic force microscopy (AFM) to image corneocyte nanotexture.

Tape stripping is a simple, non-invasive way to sample skin for research on the skin barrier.

#TapeStripping #AFM #SkinBarrier #Corneocytes

videos.t: DIY Atomic Force Microscope for Kids: Expo 2025 Osaka Best Practice Presentation (Japanese)
videos.desc:
Can school kids explore the nanoscale? This Expo 2025 Osaka Best Practice presentation (in Japanese) introduces a DIY atomic force microscope (AFM) that young people assemble themselves, like building blocks, from affordable parts with an Arduino controller, a DVD optical pickup and a piezo buzzer scanner.

Selected as one of only 25 Best Practice winners from 2000+ global teams. While PhD students struggle with $500K+ AFM systems, 8-year-olds are now exploring the nanoscale world.

videos.t: Skin Nanotexture as a Biomarker: AFM Scans and the ECTI Metric | Allergy
videos.desc:
What can the smallest details of your skin reveal about barrier damage? Atomic force microscopy (AFM) scans of the skin's outermost cells show tiny circular nano objects on corneocytes that are linked to eczema and atopic dermatitis.

This short explainer introduces the ECTI metric, which quantifies skin barrier damage from simple, non-invasive tape strips instead of biopsies, and can support early detection and treatment tracking.

Based on a 120-person study across two countries, published in Allergy. Made for dermatology researchers, clinicians and AFM newcomers curious about practical tool

videos.t: Edwin Hwu 德國台商會演講 (台灣中文)
2022 Edwin's talk at Danish Engineer Association (IDA) Full
Your skin may look fine. At the nanoscale, it may not. #Shorts
videos.desc: Your skin may look fine. At the nanoscale, it can tell a different story. We collect corneocytes with painless tape strips, scan them with an atomic force microscope and count the tiny circular nano-objects (CNOs) on them. The more severe the atopic dermatitis, the more CNOs. That count became ECTI, an objective index that tracked clinical severity in 120 people in Taiwan and Denmark. Allergy (2025): https://doi.org/10.1111/all.70170 Thanks to the LEO Foundation and the Novo Nordisk Foundation. #SkinNanotexture #AFM #AtopicDermatitis #DTU

videos.t: A kids' alarm buzzer that images atoms #Shorts
videos.desc: €0.10 piezo buzzers from a kid's personal alarm became the XYZ scanner of our low-cost AFM. No high-voltage amplifier, better linearity than a classic piezo tube, and it still resolves 0.36 nm atomic steps on graphite. From my Hackaday Europe talk. #HardwareHacking #AFM
